title: Cassandra: Enabling Reasoning LLMs at Edge via Self-Speculative Decoding
evidence_span: Cassandra is an algorithm-hardware co-designed, training-free self-speculative decoding framework for low-batch reasoning LLM inference. It constructs a draft model through fine-grained data selection, uses pruning and mantissa truncation to select salient weight and KV-cache values, and adds a lightweight encoder-decoder hardware module to reduce format-conversion overhead when integrating with commercial GPUs and NPUs. The paper reports up to 2.41x speedup over BF16 and 1.81x more tokens than Eagle-3 under the same memory budget on Llama 3 8B with an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090.
problem: Reasoning LLMs incur high decode-stage overhead at the edge, while existing self-speculative decoding methods can have weak low-batch performance or require additional training; representation-conversion overhead also limits practical deployment.
method_or_artifact: A training-free self-speculative decoding pipeline using fine-grained data selection, pruning, mantissa truncation, salient weight/KV-cache selection, and a lightweight hardware encoder-decoder for format conversion.
workload_or_benchmark: Reasoning LLM inference, including Llama 3 8B on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090, evaluated in low-batch edge-style decoding scenarios.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Commercial GPU/NPU integration with a lightweight format-conversion module; exact area, frequency, power, supported formats, acceptance-rate behavior, and broader device coverage require full-paper verification.
baselines: prior layer-skipping and structured KV-compression methods
metrics: 1.81x more tokens than Eagle-3 at the same memory budget
limits: The evidence is an author preprint abstract; exact quality/acceptance measurements, prompt and batch distributions, hardware area and power, format support, and generalization beyond Llama 3 8B and the RTX 4090 remain to be verified from the full paper.
